The test image shows two corn stalk sections with striking dark blue-black coloration on the outer rind, mottled with patches of lighter yellowish-tan tissue. This is a stalk disease. Key features:
- Jet-black to dark blue-black outer stalk discoloration
- Mottled pattern with lighter patches interspersed
- Concentrated on the internode surfaces
- Dried leaf sheaths at nodes

Top candidates: **Anthracnose_stalk_rot** (shiny black outer stalk) or **Tar_spot** (black structures on leaf). Let me check references.
Tar_spot is leaf-based — doesn't match. The Anthracnose_stalk_rot reference shows some darkening but I need to compare more carefully. Let me check additional candidates.

Charcoal shows internal fibrous shredding, Diplodia shows tan/straw stalks. Neither match the prominent dark outer rind coloration in the test image. The test image shows jet-black outer stalk discoloration — hallmark of Anthracnose_stalk_rot.

Let me view two more references to complete my budget.

Physoderma_stalk_rot shows localized dark node necrosis with a "pinched" appearance. Bacterial_stalk_rot shows wilting and water-soaked node lesions. Neither matches.

**Analysis summary:**
- Test image: two corn stalk sections with **jet-black to dark blue-black outer rind discoloration**, mottled with lighter yellowish-tan patches across the internode surfaces
- Anthracnose_stalk_rot description perfectly matches: "shiny, jet-black to dark brown discoloration of the outer stalk tissue, particularly concentrated at and between the nodes, giving the lower stalk internodes a distinctly darkened, glazed appearance"
- All other stalk rots (Charcoal = internal fibrous pith with pepper-like sclerotia; Diplodia = straw-colored stalks with small pycnidia; Physoderma = localized node pinching; Bacterial = water-soaked node with wilting) show distinctly different patterns
- The characteristic external black glazing of the rind is the definitive identifier

Other stalk rots were ruled out: Charcoal rot shows internal fibrous pith with pepper-like microsclerotia; Diplodia shows straw-colored stalks with small black pycnidia; Physoderma shows localized node-pinching necrosis; Bacterial shows water-soaked node collapse with wilting foliage. None exhibit this distinctive external jet-black rind discoloration."}
